para: add the leek tops to a large pot with the water, thyme, garlic, salt, and peppercorns.
optional_instructions.title: prep broth

para: bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
optional_instructions.title: boil and simmer

para: strain and measure 1440mL broth for the soup.
optional_instructions.title: strain and measure

para: freeze the remaining broth or store it in the refrigerator for another use.
optional_instructions.title: package and freeze

para: chop dark green tops off leeks.
cut leeks in half lengthwise, wash well.
slice leeks into semi-circles, onion into crescents.
instructions.title: cut leeks

para: melt the butter over medium heat in a large soup pot.
add the leeks, onion and garlic and cook, stirring regularly, until soft and wilted, about 10 minutes.
lower the heat if they start to brown.
instructions.title: sauté vegetables

para: add the potatoes, broth, bay leaves, thyme, salt and pepper to pot and bring to a boil.
cover and turn the heat down to low.
simmer for 15 minutes, or until the potatoes are very soft.
instructions.title: simmer soup

para: remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
purée the soup with a hand-held immersion blender until smooth.
or blend in batches in a standard blender (see note).
optional: strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
add the heavy cream and bring to a simmer.
season with salt and pepper to taste.
too thin: simmer to reduce. too thick: add water or stock.
garnish with chives.
instructions.title: blend and serve

notes.title: Blender
notes.para: if using a standard blender to purée the soup: be sure not to fill the jar more than halfway; leave the hole in the lid open and cover loosely with a dishtowel to allow the heat to escape; and pour blended soup into a clean pot

notes.title: Freezer Friendly Instructions
notes.para: the soup can be frozen, without the cream, for up to 3 months. defrost the soup in the refrigerator for 12 hours and then reheat it on the stovetop over medium heat until hot. once heated through, add the cream and bring to a simmer before serving.

para: add shrimp to a bowl.
add salt, cajun seasoning, italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika, then mix.
instructions.title: season shrimp

para: add olive oil to a pan over medium-high heat, add shrimp and cook, flipping after 2-3 minutes.
remove from the pan and set aside.
instructions.title: cook shrimp

para: cook the linguine in salted boiling water following the package instructions.
drain, then toss with the sauce once it's ready.
instructions.title: cook linguine

para: add a little extra olive oil and the butter to the pan, then the shallot, over medium heat.
after 2 minutes, add the garlic and red pepper flakes or chili pepper.
deglaze with the broth or white wine, and boil the liquid down to about 1/3 of the original amount.
add the cream and parmesan, and cook the cream down until the sauce thickens.
add more seasoning to taste.
add the lemon juice.
add the shrimp.
instructions.title: make sauce

para: serve with extra parmesan, parsley, and pepper.
instructions.title: serve

notes.title: Cream
notes.para: the cream is optional; without it you get a lighter, brothier sauce.

para: season the chicken with avocado oil and cajun seasoning.
cook in a pan over medium-high heat to an internal temperature of 68°C (155°F).
remove from the pan and set aside, keeping the pan for the vegetables.
instructions.title: season and cook chicken

para: add the bell pepper, onion, garlic, jalapeño, shallot, pepper, and sun-dried tomatoes to a food processor.
pulse until roughly diced, not a paste or liquid.
bring a pot of water to a boil and add salt, then cook the linguine following the package instructions.
instructions.title: pulse vegetables

para: add avocado oil to the chicken pan.
add ¾ of the vegetable mixture to the pan and season with salt.
when the vegetables are wilted and fragrant, add the cream, parmesan, and cajun seasoning.
instructions.title: make sauce

para: drain the linguine, saving the pasta water, and toss it in the sauce with some of the pasta water.
chop the chicken.
add the remaining vegetable mixture to another pan with avocado oil, and when fragrant add the chicken and butter.
instructions.title: add pasta

para: place the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, lemon zest, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper in a jar and shake well to combine.
optional_instructions.title: shake dressing

para: bring the water, butter, and a pinch of salt to a boil.
add the couscous, stir, and cover.
remove from the heat and let sit for 5 minutes.
instructions.title: cook couscous

para: meanwhile, make the dressing.
instructions.title: make dressing

para: place the couscous in a large bowl and fluff with a fork.
allow to cool completely.
instructions.title: cool couscous

para: add the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, feta, parsley, mint, basil, oregano, and dressing.
toss to combine and serve.
instructions.title: toss and serve

notes.title: Substitutions
notes.para: use cooked quinoa or rice instead of couscous if you prefer. add any fresh or roasted vegetables; chopped spinach or kale are delicious additions.

notes.title: Olive Oil
notes.para: use a light-tasting olive oil, as some extra virgin olive oils can taste bitter. any oil you have on hand works too: try vegetable, grapeseed, or canola oil.

para: mix the hot sauce, mayonnaise, and black pepper together.
optional_instructions.title: mix aioli

para: add the buttermilk to a large bowl.
add the pickle juice, bouillon cube, kosher salt, garlic powder, chili powder, and paprika, then mix.
add the chicken thighs, fully submerged in the buttermilk.
marinate for 1-8 hours, or overnight.
instructions.title: buttermilk marinade

para: add the flour, then mix in the corn starch, onion powder, kosher salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
remove the chicken thighs from the buttermilk marinade and lay them in the dredge.
thoroughly coat the chicken thighs in the dredge, dip them back in the buttermilk, and dredge once more.
instructions.title: flour dredge

para: fill a deep pan with canola oil, a few inches deep.
start heating on high, then lower to medium as it heats.
check the heat with a small splash of water on the oil; it should steam and sizzle.
do not add the chicken thighs until the oil reaches roughly 175°C (350°F).
submerge the chicken thighs in the oil for 6-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
once removed, let the chicken thighs sit for a few minutes before serving.
instructions.title: fry in canola oil

para: spread piri-piri aioli on the buns, then add lettuce and a chicken thigh.
instructions.title: assemble sandwiches

para: mix the protein, soy sauce, and sugar.
for lean cuts like chicken breast or pork loin, add about 10 mL of water.
instructions.title: marinate protein

para: if the rice noodles are stuck together, peel them apart into individual strands (if they're cold and hard, see the cold noodles note).
divide the rice noodles into portions, since you'll cook one portion at a time (225 g per portion).
instructions.title: prepare noodles

para: stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, golden mountain sauce, and black soy sauce together.
divide the sauce evenly into portions, about 20 mL each.
instructions.title: mix sauce

para: thinly slice the stems on a bias and roughly chop the leaves.
instructions.title: prep chinese broccoli

para: heat 7.5 mL of the vegetable oil in a well-seasoned wok or large cast iron skillet over high heat.
when hot, add all of the protein and spread it into a single layer.
sear until browned underneath, then toss until fully cooked.
remove from the pan and set aside.
instructions.title: sear protein

para: from here on, cook one portion at a time.
with the heat still off, add 22 mL of vegetable oil and one portion of garlic to the wok, then turn the heat to medium-high.
stir until the smallest bits of garlic start to turn golden.
instructions.title: cook garlic

para: add the egg, break the yolk, and let it set about halfway, then scramble briefly.
instructions.title: add egg

para: add the chinese broccoli and toss to coat it in the oil, about 10-15 seconds.
instructions.title: add chinese broccoli

para: add one portion of rice noodles, one portion of the sauce, and the 10 mL of sugar.
turn the heat up to high and toss to coat the noodles evenly in the sauce, taking care not to cut the noodles with your spatula.
instructions.title: add noodles and sauce

para: once coated, spread the rice noodles across the pan and leave them for 15-30 seconds, until some have charred.
flip or toss the rice noodles and let them sit again to char the other side.
optional: flip a couple more times for extra char.
instructions.title: char noodles

para: add one portion of the cooked protein back to the pan, leaving behind any juices, and toss briefly to mix.
turn off the heat.
instructions.title: add protein

para: plate the noodles, then quickly wipe the pan clean with a paper towel and cook the next portion.
instructions.title: plate and repeat

para: sprinkle with ground white pepper and serve with chili vinegar.
instructions.title: serve

notes.title: One Portion at a Time
notes.para: cooking one portion at a time is more work, but well worth it. too many noodles in the wok trap steam, which overcooks them and stops them from charring, and that char is the iconic toasty flavour.

notes.title: Cold Noodles
notes.para: if your rice noodles are cold and stuck together, don't peel them apart cold. divide them into smaller chunks as best you can, spread them on a plate, and microwave for 1 minute. separate them further, then microwave for another minute. repeat until the noodles are hot and soft enough to peel apart.

notes.title: Black Soy Sauce
notes.para: black soy sauce adds the dark colour and rich flavour iconic to pad see ew. if you can't find it, use the same amount of chinese dark soy sauce and leave out the golden mountain sauce, since chinese dark soy is much saltier than thai black soy. if it needs more salt, add a little soy sauce or fish sauce at the table.

para: bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the pasta following the package instructions.
preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F).
instructions.title: boil water and preheat oven

para: add the butter to a pan.
sweat the shallot in the pan for a few minutes.
add the flour, mustard powder, and paprika, and keep stirring.
instructions.title: make roux

para: add the milk, bay leaves, white pepper, and nutmeg.
bring to a simmer while whisking.
instructions.title: thicken sauce

para: turn the heat to its lowest setting and add a couple of cups of shredded cheese: the cheddar, asiago, gouda, and parmesan.
once the cheese has melted, add the pasta to the sauce and stir.
instructions.title: add cheeses

para: top with more cheddar, the bread crumbs, and parmesan.
bake for 10-15 minutes, then broil for 30 seconds.
season with salt to taste.
instructions.title: bake

para: preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F) and line a rimmed baking sheet with a silicone mat or foil.
arrange the salmon skin-side down on the baking sheet.
instructions.title: prepare salmon

para: in a small bowl, combine the parsley, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
instructions.title: make marinade

para: spread the marinade generously over the top and sides of the salmon, then top each piece with a slice of lemon.
instructions.title: top salmon

para: bake at 230°C (450°F) for 12-15 minutes, until just cooked through and flaky.
instructions.title: bake

para: blend the anchovies, garlic, capers, dry mustard, worcestershire sauce, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, and honey together.
instructions.title: blend dressing

para: slowly stream in the olive oil while blending until creamy.
instructions.title: add oil

para: stir in half of the parmesan, and save the other half for the top.
instructions.title: add parmesan

para: blend the egg yolk, dijon mustard, anchovies, garlic, worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, and salt together.
instructions.title: blend dressing

para: slowly stream in the olive oil while blending, then mix in the mayonnaise.
instructions.title: add oil and mayonnaise

para: stir in the parmesan.
instructions.title: add parmesan

para: toss with romaine lettuce and top with crisped prosciutto and sourdough croutons.
instructions.title: serve

para: preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F).
line a large baking sheet with aluminum foil.
instructions.title: preheat oven

para: add the salt, garlic powder, onion powder, italian seasoning, black pepper, and paprika to a bowl.
drizzle the olive oil over the chicken thighs, then sprinkle the spice mix on both sides.
instructions.title: season chicken

para: bake for 35-45 minutes.
instructions.title: bake

para: heat the avocado oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
add the green beans, salt, and pepper.
instructions.title: sear beans

para: cook, stirring often, until the beans soften, about 5 minutes.
instructions.title: cook beans

para: reduce the heat to low and stir in the hot sauce, garlic, and honey.
stir until the beans are tender-crisp and coated in sauce, 1-3 more minutes.
serve immediately.
instructions.title: add sauce

para: melt the butter.
heat the milk in a small pot over medium heat until it simmers.
combine the flour, cocoa powder, sugar, and eggs in a bowl with a mixer.
gradually add the melted butter and hot milk, mixing as you go.
instructions.title: make crepe batter

para: whip the whipping cream and sugar with a mixer until fluffy.
instructions.title: make whipped cream

para: heat a crepe pan to about medium and add enough batter to cover the whole pan.
cook for 2-4 minutes, loosen the edge with a spatula, then flip.
cook for 2-3 minutes on the other side, then move to a rack to cool.
repeat until the batter is used up.
instructions.title: cook crepes

para: bring the heavy cream and sugar to a boil in a pot.
pour over the baking chocolate and butter, mixing until melted.
instructions.title: make chocolate coating

para: once the crepes have cooled to room temperature, start building.
lay a crepe on your cake plate and cover it completely with a layer of whipped cream; repeat until you run out of crepes.
slowly pour the chocolate coating over the cake, coating it in a thick layer.
instructions.title: build cake

para: preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
line a baking pan with parchment paper and set aside.
instructions.title: preheat oven

para: in a separate bowl, mix the flour, baking soda, salt, and baking powder. set aside.
instructions.title: mix dry ingredients

para: cream together the butter, sugar, and brown sugar until combined.
instructions.title: cream butter and sugar

para: beat in the eggs and vanilla extract until fluffy.
instructions.title: add eggs and vanilla

para: mix in the dry ingredients until combined.
instructions.title: combine

para: add the chocolate chips (a 340 g package) and mix well.
instructions.title: add chocolate chips

para: roll 30-45 mL portions of dough into balls (or use a small cookie scoop) and space them evenly on the baking pan.
instructions.title: shape cookies

para: bake for about 8-10 minutes, until they're just barely starting to brown.
instructions.title: bake

para: let them sit on the pan for 2 minutes before moving them to a cooling rack.
instructions.title: cool

para: add the onion, carrot, celery, jalapeño, and bell pepper to a large pot and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
instructions.title: cook vegetables

para: add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
instructions.title: add garlic

para: add the ground beef and pork sausage, breaking them apart with a spatula as they cook.
once the meat is about half browned, add the brown sugar, chili powder, cumin, and oregano, and stir well.
instructions.title: brown meat and spices

para: add the beef broth, beer, kidney beans, black beans, crushed and diced tomatoes, tomato paste, and worcestershire sauce, and stir well.
instructions.title: add liquids

para: bring to a boil and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently.
reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.title: simmer

para: serve with sour cream, shredded cheddar, and corn chips.
instructions.title: serve

para: cut the ends off the onions and remove the skins.
slice them finely from end to end.
instructions.title: chop onions

para: preheat a dutch oven over medium heat, then add the butter and vegetable oil.
add the onions and salt them generously.
cook for 10 minutes until translucent.
reduce to low heat and stir every few minutes.
cook for about 1 hour, until deep golden brown. don't let them burn.
instructions.title: cook onions

para: add the white wine and turn the heat up to medium to reduce.
the onions should mix with the white wine and become jammy.
add the flour and mix it in for 1 minute.
instructions.title: deglaze with white wine

para: add the beef broth, bay leaves, thyme, and worcestershire sauce, and bring to a simmer.
reduce to low heat, cover, and cook for about 30 minutes.
add a splash more worcestershire sauce to taste.
instructions.title: simmer soup

para: preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F).
add the baguette slices to a pan and drizzle lightly with olive oil.
bake for 5-10 minutes.
ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, float the baguette slices on top, and cover with gruyere and parmesan.
instructions.title: toast baguette

para: set the oven to broil and broil the soup for 3-5 minutes, careful not to burn the bread.
instructions.title: broil

para: whisk the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and 300 mL of the chocolate chips in a large bowl.
instructions.title: mix dry ingredients

para: whisk the eggs, cooled butter, vegetable oil, buttermilk, and greek yogurt in a medium bowl, then add the vanilla extract.
instructions.title: mix wet ingredients

para: pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and whisk gently until combined. don't over-mix.
instructions.title: combine

para: cover the bowl and let the batter rest for 45 minutes.
preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and put 12 muffin liners in a muffin tin.
instructions.title: rest batter

para: divide the batter between the liners with an ice cream scoop, slightly overfilling each one.
instructions.title: fill liners

para: top each muffin with the reserved chocolate chips and the coarse sugar.
instructions.title: add toppings

para: bake at 220°C (425°F) for 8 minutes, then reduce to 175°C (350°F) for 8-10 minutes.
they're done when a toothpick comes out clean.
instructions.title: bake

para: cool for 5-10 minutes in the pan, then 5-10 minutes on a wire rack.
instructions.title: cool

para: preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F), or 180°C fan.
instructions.title: preheat oven

para: place the potatoes in a roasting pan with the chicken stock, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, and salt, and toss well.
instructions.title: coat potatoes

para: roast for 20 minutes.
turn the potatoes and roast for another 25-30 minutes, until the liquid is mostly absorbed or evaporated and you're left mainly with oil in the pan.
instructions.title: roast

para: move the potatoes to a separate tray.
tilt the original pan, scoop off as much of the oil as you can (some juices are fine), and drizzle it over the potatoes.
roast for 35-40 minutes, turning once or twice, until golden and a bit crispy on the edges.
instructions.title: crisp potatoes (optional)

para: put the original pan with the garlic juices back in the oven for the last 5-10 minutes to reduce them and turn the garlic golden.
instructions.title: reduce pan juices (optional)

para: move the potatoes to a serving platter and drizzle with the reduced garlic pan juices, or toss the potatoes in the pan.
garnish with lemon wedges and fresh oregano if you like.
instructions.title: serve

para: place the chicken breasts in a large bowl with the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
mix well with your hands, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 30-60 minutes.
instructions.title: marinate chicken

para: cut the wooden skewers to fit your griddle pan and soak them in water so they don't burn.
thread the chicken pieces onto the skewers, not too tightly.
instructions.title: skewer chicken

para: preheat a grill or griddle pan over high heat.
cook the skewers for about 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until coloured on all sides and cooked through.
instructions.title: grill chicken

para: while the chicken cooks, preheat the oven to 250°C (480°F).
brush the pitas with olive oil on both sides and season with salt and oregano.
place a large oven tray upside down at the bottom of the oven, put the pitas on top, and bake for 2 minutes. you can also use a griddle pan or grill.
instructions.title: warm pitas

para: spread the sliced red onion on a platter and top with the skewers.
drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and a good squeeze of lemon juice.
serve warm with the pitas and tzatziki.
or wrap it like a sandwich: spread tzatziki on a pita, top with the chicken, onion, tomato, and fried potatoes, and roll it up.
instructions.title: serve

para: preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F).
instructions.title: preheat oven

para: in a small bowl, mix the onion powder, italian seasoning, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
sprinkle generously over the chicken thighs.
instructions.title: season chicken

para: heat the olive oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
add the chicken presentation-side down and cook until golden brown and it releases easily from the skillet, about 3-4 minutes per side.
remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.
instructions.title: sear chicken

para: in the same skillet, add the shallot, couscous, garlic, and thyme, and cook until the garlic is fragrant and the couscous is toasted, about 2-3 minutes.
add the chicken broth to deglaze the skillet and bring to a boil.
instructions.title: toast couscous

para: put the chicken back in the skillet, arrange the lemon slices around it, and move the skillet to the oven.
bake until the chicken is cooked through and the couscous is puffed, about 15 minutes.
instructions.title: bake

other: half a batch, or your favourite

para: preheat the oven to 165°C (325°F).
place cupcake liners in a muffin pan and spray them lightly with cooking spray.
instructions.title: prep

para: add the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and espresso powder to a large bowl and whisk to combine.
instructions.title: whisk dry ingredients

para: add the milk, vegetable oil, egg, and vanilla extract to the flour mixture and mix until well combined.
carefully add the boiling water and mix until the batter is smooth. the batter will be very thin.
instructions.title: add wet ingredients

para: divide the batter evenly between the liners, filling each about halfway.
bake for about 20 minutes, until a toothpick in the centre comes out clean.
let the cupcakes cool completely.
instructions.title: bake

para: while the cupcakes cool, make the frosting. you'll need half of the frosting recipe for a dozen cupcakes.
frost the cupcakes and serve.
instructions.title: frost and serve

notes.title: Frosting
notes.para: use half of this vanilla buttercream recipe, or another favourite frosting: https://addapinch.com/classic-vanilla-buttercream-frosting-recipe/

para: heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
add the garlic slices and sauté, stirring constantly, until golden and crisp.
set the garlic aside, pour out the excess oil, and return the pan to the stove.
instructions.title: fry garlic

para: add half of the butter.
once melted, add the fresh garlic and cook for 1.5 minutes.
instructions.title: cook butter and garlic

para: add the rice and stir to coat it in the garlic butter.
add the chicken broth, put the lid on, and bring to a boil, then immediately turn down to medium-low.
cook for 12-15 minutes, until the rice has absorbed all the liquid (tilt the pan to check).
take the pan off the heat, leave the lid on, and rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.title: cook rice

para: fluff with a fork and move to a serving bowl.
stir through the remaining butter and the green onions.
sprinkle with the crispy garlic, salt, and white pepper, and serve.
instructions.title: serve

name: focaccia
equipment: 33 x 23 cm baking pan or 46 x 33 cm rimmed baking sheet

para: whisk the active dry yeast, honey, and water in a medium bowl and let sit for 5 minutes.
it should foam or at least turn creamy. if it doesn't, the yeast is dead and you should start again.
instructions.title: activate yeast

para: add the flour and kosher salt and mix with a rubber spatula until a shaggy dough forms and no dry streaks remain.
instructions.title: make dough

para: pour 60 mL of the olive oil into a big bowl that fits in your fridge.
move the dough into the bowl and turn it to coat in the oil.
cover with plastic wrap and chill until doubled in size, at least 8 hours and up to 1 day.
or let it rise at room temperature until doubled, 3-4 hours.
instructions.title: refrigerate overnight

para: generously butter a 33 x 23 cm baking pan for thicker focaccia, or a 46 x 33 cm rimmed baking sheet for thinner, crispier focaccia.
pour 15 mL of the olive oil into the centre of the pan.

keeping the dough in the bowl, use a fork in each hand to lift the edge farthest from you up and over into the centre. give the bowl a quarter turn and repeat. do this 2 more times to deflate the dough while forming a rough ball.
move the dough to the pan, pour any oil left in the bowl over it, and turn the dough to coat.
let rise uncovered in a warm, dry spot until doubled in size, at least 1½ hours and up to 4 hours.
instructions.title: fold and rise

para: preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F).
poke the dough to check it's ready: it should spring back slowly and leave a small dent. if it springs back quickly, it isn't ready yet.
lightly oil your hands. on a rimmed baking sheet, gently stretch the dough to fill it (you probably won't need to in a baking pan).
dimple the focaccia all over with your fingers, pressing all the way to the bottom of the pan.
drizzle with the remaining 15 mL of olive oil and sprinkle with the flaky sea salt.
add the shallot, garlic, rosemary, and oregano.
bake for 20-30 minutes, until puffed and golden brown all over.
instructions.title: top and bake

para: once the focaccia is out of the oven, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
grate in the garlic with a microplane.
cook, stirring often, until the garlic is just lightly toasted, 30-45 seconds.
brush onto the fresh focaccia.
instructions.title: garlic butter (optional)

para: whisk the eggs, pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
set aside.
instructions.title: make egg mixture

para: cook the guanciale over medium heat until crisp, then set it aside.
add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then set aside.
instructions.title: cook guanciale and garlic

para: cook the spaghetti in salted water following the package instructions, until al dente.
drain, saving 240 mL of the pasta water.
instructions.title: cook pasta

para: add the hot spaghetti to the pan with the garlic and toss to coat.
quickly take it off the heat and add the egg mixture.
mix well with tongs, adding pasta water if needed.
stir in the guanciale.
garnish with parsley and more pecorino.
instructions.title: mix pasta
